title: High-resolution mass spectrometry
keyIdea: A high-resolution mass spectrometer measures the m/z of the molecular ion, M⁺, to four decimal places. Isotope masses are not whole numbers, apart from ¹²C, which is exactly 12 because it defines the atomic mass unit: ¹H is 1.007825, ¹⁴N is 14.003074 and ¹⁶O is 15.994915. So formulae with the same nominal mass have different accurate masses: CO is 27.9949, N₂ is 28.0061 and C₂H₄ is 28.0313. Add up the isotope masses for each candidate formula and choose the one that matches the measured M⁺. A low-resolution instrument rounds all three to 28 and cannot tell them apart.
familyTip: Ask your teen to explain why 28 is not enough to name a gas. Then give them a measured mass like 44.0262 and let them work out, with a calculator, whether it is CO₂, C₃H₈ or C₂H₄O.

visual.caption: Which accurate mass belongs to which formula? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: drag formulas to their accurate-mass peaks, build a formula to hit M⁺, find the decimal places that split a set, match spectra, spot the slip.

kid: A normal mass spectrum gives the molecular ion, M⁺, as a whole number. CO, N₂ and C₂H₄ all show up at 28. So you cannot tell which gas you have.
A high-resolution machine reads m/z to four decimal places. It can do this because atoms do not weigh whole numbers. Only carbon-12 is exactly 12. It sets the unit.
Hydrogen-1 is 1.007825. Nitrogen-14 is 14.003074. Oxygen-16 is 15.994915. Add them up for each formula. CO is 27.9949, N₂ is 28.0061 and C₂H₄ is 28.0313.
To find a formula, list the ones that fit the whole number. Work out each accurate mass. The one that matches the measured M⁺ is your answer.
adult: Ages 17 to 18: A-level Chemistry, for example AQA 7405 section 3.3.6.2, where a molecular formula is found from a precise M⁺ value. Students are given isotope masses and must sum them for each candidate. The lab uses the NIST values for ¹H, ¹⁴N and ¹⁶O, with ¹²C exactly 12 by definition. Exam papers often give 4 d.p. values (1.0078, 14.0031, 15.9949), which can move the last digit: C₃H₆O is 58.0417 with those, 58.0419 here.

Nominal mass uses whole numbers, so many formulae share one value. Accurate masses differ because of the mass defect: each ¹H adds 0.0078 above 1, and ¹⁶O is 0.0051 below 16. Swapping CH₄ for O therefore lowers the mass by 0.0364, which is why C₂H₄O (44.0262) sits 0.0364 below C₃H₈ (44.0626). The mass of the lost electron, 0.00055, is ignored at this level.

Common mistakes: using average relative atomic masses (H 1.008, C 12.011) instead of isotope masses; rounding the sum to a whole number; miscounting atoms; and reading the base peak or the small M+1 peak as M⁺. Some learners think ¹²C is 12 because it is rounded. It is exact by definition, while every other isotope mass has decimals. HRMS gives the formula, not the structure, so it cannot tell isomers apart.

In the lab you drag CO, N₂ and C₂H₄ onto their peaks and build three formulae with + and − to hit a measured M⁺. You drag a decimal-places dial to see when a set of formulae splits apart, match four spectra, and find the slip in four worked sums.

practice.prompt: M⁺ is measured at 44.0262. Which formula is it?
practice.hint: Work out 2(12) + 4(1.007825) + 15.994915 and compare it with the other two.
practice.explain: C₂H₄O = 44.0262. CO₂ = 43.9898 and C₃H₈ = 44.0626, so only C₂H₄O matches.

practice.prompt: Each ¹H atom is 1.0078 to 4 d.p., which is 0.0078 above 1. How many ten-thousandths (units of 0.0001) above {n} is the mass of {n} hydrogen atoms?
practice.hint: Each hydrogen adds 78 ten-thousandths. Multiply by the number of atoms.
practice.explain: {n} × 0.0078 = {n} × 78 ten-thousandths = {=78*n}. That is why formulae with many hydrogens sit above their nominal mass.

practice.prompt: Why is the isotope mass of ¹²C exactly 12?
choices: The atomic mass unit is defined as 1/12 of a ¹²C atom.
It is rounded to a whole number.
practice.hint: Think about how the unit is defined.
practice.explain: The unified atomic mass unit is 1/12 of the mass of a ¹²C atom, so ¹²C is 12 by definition. Other isotope masses have decimals.

practice.prompt: An alkane CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ has n = {n}. What is its nominal (whole-number) mass?
practice.hint: Use C = 12 and H = 1, then count 2n + 2 hydrogens.
practice.explain: 12 × {n} + (2 × {n} + 2) × 1 = {=14*n+2}. Its accurate mass is a little higher, because each H is 1.007825.

practice.prompt: A low-resolution spectrum shows M⁺ at 28. Why can it not tell CO from N₂?
practice.hint: What happens to 27.9949 and 28.0061 when they are rounded?
practice.explain: Rounded to a whole number, both are 28. Only a high-resolution reading shows 27.9949 against 28.0061.

pool.prompt: Which is the accurate mass of N₂?
pool.hint: Use the ¹⁴N isotope mass, 14.003074, not the average Ar.

pool.prompt: M⁺ is at 58.0419. Which formula fits?
pool.hint: All three have nominal mass 58. Work out each accurate mass.

pool.prompt: Which hydrogen mass should you use in a high-resolution calculation?
pool.hint: HRMS measures single isotopes, not an average.
pool.explain: 1.007825 is the ¹H isotope mass. 1.008 is the average Ar, which includes some ²H.

pool.prompt: Which peak is used to find the molecular formula?
pool.hint: Which peak is the whole molecule minus an electron?
pool.explain: M⁺ is the molecular ion. The base peak is just the tallest, often a fragment, and M+1 comes from ¹³C.

pool.prompt: Each ¹⁶O atom is 15.9949, which is 0.0051 below 16. A compound has {o} oxygen atoms. How many ten-thousandths (units of 0.0001) below {o} × 16 is their total mass?
pool.hint: Each oxygen is 51 ten-thousandths below 16. Multiply by the number of oxygens.
pool.explain: {o} × 51 = {=51*o} ten-thousandths below. That is why oxygen-rich formulae like CO₂ sit below their nominal mass.

pool.prompt: A student writes C: 3 × 12.011 for propane. What is the slip?
choices: 12.011 is the average Ar, not the ¹²C isotope mass.
pool.explain: In HRMS use ¹²C = 12 exactly. 12.011 includes ¹³C, so it is the average Ar.

pool.prompt: Which pair can a low-resolution instrument tell apart?
pool.hint: Which pair has different whole-number masses?
pool.explain: 46 and 44 are different nominal masses. The other pairs both round to 28 or 44.

pool.prompt: Swapping CH₄ for O in a formula changes the accurate mass by about how much?
pool.explain: 16.0313 − 15.9949 = 0.0364, so the O version is 0.0364 lighter, as in C₂H₄O against C₃H₈.

pool.prompt: A molecule has {c} carbon atoms and nothing else in its formula is carbon. What do the carbons add to its accurate mass?
pool.hint: ¹²C is exactly 12, so multiply the number of carbons by 12.
pool.explain: {c} × 12 = {=12*c}, exactly, since ¹²C has no decimals.

pool.prompt: M⁺ is at 30.0106. Which formula is it?
